cards.title: Chains of elif
cards.body: Python checks each condition from top to bottom and stops at the first True one. Order your checks from the highest value to the lowest.

hi.title: elif ki chain
hi.body: Python har condition upar se neeche check karta hai aur pehli True wali par ruk jaata hai. Checks ko sabse badi value se sabse chhoti tak rakho.

cards.title: Why the order matters
cards.body: If the `>= 50` check came first, a speed of 120 would print okay and never reach the fast check. The first match wins.

hi.title: Order kyun matter karta hai
hi.body: Agar `>= 50` wala check pehle aata, toh 120 ki speed okay print karti aur fast wale check tak kabhi nahi pahunchti. Pehla match jeet jaata hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: For 40 degrees it prints `warm`, never `hot`. Tap the line that checks too early.

bug.fix: The first true check wins, and 40 is already `>= 20`. Check the higher limit first: `if temp >= 35`, then `elif temp >= 20`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: 40 degrees ke liye yeh `warm` print karta hai, `hot` kabhi nahi. Us line par tap karo jo bahut jaldi check karti hai.
hi.fix: Pehla true check jeet jaata hai, aur 40 pehle hi `>= 20` hai. Badi limit pehle check karo: `if temp >= 35`, phir `elif temp >= 20`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: score >= 50 is True first, so Python prints pass and skips every branch below it.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: score >= 50 sabse pehle True hota hai, isliye Python pass print karta hai aur neeche ki har branch chhod deta hai.

exercise.prompt: Read a score from 0 to 100 and print its letter grade: `A` for 90 or more, `B` for 80 to 89, `C` for 70 to 79, `D` for 60 to 69, and `F` below 60.
